title: Embedding & Reranker Regression Sentinel for Config and Model Changes
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Build an automated quality sentinel that ties embedding and reranker model/config changes to offline regression checks and lightweight online canary signals. The sentinel will gate merges and deploys when a proposed model or configuration change (quantization profile, batch strategy, reranker weights) causes measurable degradation on key retrieval metrics.

Background: We currently run one-off offline evals for embedding/reranker releases, but lack a standard gating mechanism integrated into PRs and deploys. This ticket implements a reproducible offline harness, a set of thresholds/KPIs, and an optional canary path in runtime to collect incremental online signals for high-risk rollouts.

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- Offline eval harness: a reproducible job that takes a model/config artifact and a named eval-suite and produces a deterministic report (recall@10, precision@10, MRR@5, nDCG@10, mean cosine drift) and a single verdict (pass/warn/fail) based on thresholds and statistical tests.
- Canary pipeline: when a PR targets runtime/model config, CI can optionally create a canary deployment (10% traffic) with telemetry to compute online reranker metrics (click-through proxy, freshness) and embedding drift (cosine distribution shift). Canary must be kill-switchable and auto-fall back on fail.
- Gating: PR comment with link to eval report; if verdict==fail block merge or require owner override with justification. Provide an API for manual override and for opt-outs (e.g., experimental branches).
- Dashboards & alerts: Grafana dashboard for historical trend of eval metrics by model+config; Slack alerting on failed eval or drift > alert threshold.
- Documentation: Confluence runbook describing how to author eval suites, acceptable thresholds, and how to interpret p-values and effect sizes.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Thresholding: use bootstrap confidence intervals for recall/precision deltas vs baseline instead of pure absolute thresholds to reduce false positives from small test suites. Trade-off: additional computation time for bootstrapping.
- Sampling: to keep compute cost reasonable, offline harness will sample a stratified subset of production queries (time + user cohort) by default. Trade-off: small sampling may miss low-frequency regressions — mitigation: provide a full-run option for major releases.
- Drift metric: measure cosine similarity distribution and summarize with mean and 90th-percentile; compute KL-divergence over binned similarity histograms for sensitivity to distributional shifts.
- Privacy: eval datasets must be scrubbed for PII; avoid exporting raw user queries in artifacts. Use hashed identifiers and synthetic augmentations when needed.

Implementation plan:
1) Eval harness (week 1-2): create a reproducible job in the evals repo that accepts model artifact + config + eval-suite id. Output JSON report and HTML summary. (ref: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/214)
2) Thresholds & stats (week 2): implement bootstrap test, KL drift, and automated verdict logic. Store baseline metrics in a small metadata datastore (S3 + manifest).
3) CI/PR integration (week 3): GitHub Action that triggers harness on model/config PRs and posts report link. If verdict==fail comment and set check to failed.
4) Canary runtime hook (week 3-4): add lightweight canary route and a telemetry aggregator that computes online proxies and returns an immediate canary_verdict. (ref: CD PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1492)
5) Dashboards & alerts (week 4): create Grafana panels and PagerDuty/Slack alerting for failed evals or drift spikes.

Acceptance tests:
- Run harness on synthetic regression where reranker weights are scrambled; expect fail verdict with delta_recall@10 > 5% and p<0.01.
- Simulate benign quantization change with no metric regression; expect pass or warn.
- Canary abort: when canary returns fail, traffic must roll back within 2 minutes.

Risks and mitigations:
- False positives from small eval sets: provide mechanism to increase sample size and require manual review when dataset small.
- Cost of running full-harness on every PR: by default run lightweight sample; only run full-harness on protected branches or when labeled "full-eval".
- Data leakage: enforce scrub pipeline and require security sign-off for eval-suite definitions.

Next steps / open questions:
- Define "eval-suite" ownership and retention policy for baseline metrics (how long to keep baselines and when to refresh).
- Decide threshold values for recall/precision deltas across different products (search vs semantic matching). PM input required.
- Should canary be available for Hosted-only, or also for Dedicated customers? (Operational complexity vs safety.)
